decisionSource: The issuer's own current publication: the Vermont Judiciary statewide forms library, its Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs self-help page, and the form binary that page serves; read against the integrated Vermont legal-design memo, the regenerated track-source audit, the authoritative blocker ledger, the official-PDF source assignment projection, and the adopted Master Library Edition 1.2 authority asset.
whatThisDocumentIs: The decision record that settles the Vermont fee-waiver application's source identity. Two questions were open. First, whether the controlling form number is 600-00228 or 600-00229, which the Vermont Judiciary's own materials answer inconsistently. Second, what the exact current document behind that number is. This record answers both from the issuer's publication rather than by assuming either number, states the document's role, revision, scope, official URL and exact measured bytes, records the supersession of an older revision that is still reachable at a legacy path, and names what remains before the Vermont official-PDF family can be called source-complete. It does not amend the integrated Vermont memo, does not create a source receipt, does not regenerate a registry or projection, and does not implement a renderer.

scopeOfThisJob.note: The job's stop condition reserves memo amendment, source receipts, registry regeneration and implementation to other owners. Everything this record establishes is stated here and applied elsewhere by Session A at integration.

questionPresented.conflictAsReported: The integrated Vermont memo records that the Judiciary's expungement narrative names the fee-waiver form 600-00229 while 600-00229 does not resolve at the Judiciary's document path and 600-00228 does. The memo carried the conflict without resolving it and read the 600-00228 footer as 11/2019. The Master Library manifest row, acquired against a request for 600-00229, asserts the current form is 600-00228 at revision 04/2026. This job settles the number, the revision, and the exact document.

evidence.result: No results matched the search criteria.

Returns the single row 'Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs' / '600-00228', whose download link is /sites/default/files/documents/600-00228 – Application to Waive Filing Fees & Service Costs_0.pdf. The same query shape therefore does return a result when the number exists, which is what makes the 600-00229 negative meaningful.
Not found. The sibling probe of the same path shape for 600-00228 returns HTTP 200 with a PDF.

Zero captures, on both vermontjudiciary.org and vtcourts.gov, for any URL containing 600-00229, across the whole index. The identical query for 600-00228 returns captures from 2020 through 2025 including an Arabic-language edition of the same form, so the index does cover this issuer and this form series. There is therefore no archived state in which 600-00229 was a published Vermont Judiciary document, which is what distinguishes a numbering error from a retired form.

The expungement narrative page is the sole official source of the 600-00229 number. Its exact prose is 'Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs form (600-00229)'. The hyperlink on that same reference points to https://www.vermontjudiciary.org/self-help/application-waive-filing-fees-and-service-costs, which is the Judiciary's own fee-waiver page and which names the form (600-00228). The issuer's own link therefore resolves its own prose against itself: the narrative carries a stale or mistyped number and points at the correct document.

form600_00229.conclusion: 600-00229 is not, and so far as the official record shows never has been, a published Vermont Judiciary form. It is an incorrect number appearing in the prose of one Judiciary narrative page, which itself links to the correct form. No Vermont track or component may be bound to 600-00229.

That reading is accurate for the binary at the legacy static path https://www.vtcourts.gov/sites/default/files/documents/600-00228.pdf, which still returns HTTP 200 and still carries the 11/2019 footer. role.roleBasis: The document is completed and signed only by the applicant. Section 5 is headed 'Signatures and Declaration' and carries exactly one signature block, 'Applicant Signature', with 'Printed Name' beneath it. A full text extraction of both pages returns no order recital, no decretal language, no court-findings block, no judge or clerk signature line and no grant/deny disposition. It is therefore a participant instrument and must not be mapped into a petition slot, an order slot, a stipulation slot or an instructions slot.

scope.statewideBasis: The form is published in the Judiciary's statewide forms library rather than by a single unit, and its own two dropdown fields enumerate the whole state: Division offers Civil, Criminal, Environmental, Family, Judicial Bureau and Probate; Unit offers all fourteen Vermont counties — Addison, Bennington, Caledonia, Chittenden, Essex, Franklin, Grand Isle, Lamoille, Orange, Orleans, Rutland, Washington, Windsor and Windham. A single binary is used in every division and every unit.

authorityLevel.waiverAuthority: 32 V.S.A. § 1431(h): 'Pursuant to Vermont Rules of Civil Procedure 3.1 or Vermont Rules of Appellate Procedure 24(a), part or all of the filing fee may be waived if the court finds that the applicant is unable to pay it. The clerk of the court or the clerk's designee shall establish the in forma pauperis fee in accordance with procedures and guidelines established by administrative order of the Supreme Court.'
authorityLevel.issuerDirection: The Judiciary's own fee-waiver page states: 'When you file a court case, you must either pay the filing fee or ask to have the fee waived. To ask to waive the fees, fill out and file the Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs' and identifies it as (600-00228).
authorityLevel.issuerFormsCaveat: The Judiciary's about-court-forms page states 'There isn't a court form for everything' and contemplates drafted or adapted documents, so no Vermont form may be asserted as mandatory purely because the Judiciary publishes it.
authorityLevel.conclusion: The waiver right is conferred by rule, not by this form; the statute prescribes no form number. 600-00228 is the issuer's single published statewide instrument for exercising that right and is controlling as such. It is not established as mandatory by rule or administrative order, and this record does not assert that it is. Its use in the Vermont packets stays conditional exactly as the adopted design has it.

requiredQuestions.q: What is the relationship between them?
requiredQuestions.a: A numbering typo. 600-00229 is an incorrect number for 600-00228, appearing only in the prose of the Judiciary's expungement narrative page, whose own hyperlink resolves to the fee-waiver page that names 600-00228. They are not separate documents, not a petition and order pair, not old and new revisions, not a retired form and its replacement, not language variants, and not unrelated forms.

600-00228 is 'Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs'; the printed footer uses the ampersand short form 'Application to Waive Filing Fees & Service Costs'. 600-00229 has no title because it has no document.
The Vermont Judiciary publishes 600-00228 for the Vermont Superior Court. No body publishes 600-00229.

requiredQuestions.q: Which Vermont tracks and components use it?
requiredQuestions.a: Seven tracks and seven components, each in the fee_waiver_application role: vt_exp_decriminalized, vt_seal_misdemeanor, vt_seal_felony, vt_seal_dui, vt_seal_nonconviction, vt_seal_18_to_21 and vt_seal_pardon.

requiredQuestions.q: Is it mandatory, controlling, optional, or a drafting reference?
requiredQuestions.a: Controlling as the issuer's single published statewide instrument for a fee waiver, and conditional in use. The waiver right comes from V.R.C.P. 3.1 and V.R.A.P. 24(a) through 32 V.S.A. § 1431(h); no statute or rule prescribes the form by number, and the Judiciary's about-court-forms page declines to treat its forms as exhaustive. It is not asserted here as mandatory.

requiredQuestions.q: Does resolving this identity alone make rcap-vt-acroform-fill source-complete?
requiredQuestions.a: Not by itself, and this record does not claim it. 600-00228 is the only entry in that job's unresolvedOrTerminalIdentities, and its own two implementation identities, 200-00129 and 200-00132A, are already exact_source_requirement_ready with materialization receipts. But the projection derives unresolved_identity for this key from repository_measurement_unavailable, which is a mechanical consequence of the adopted edition manifesting the asset as supporting_process with packetCandidate false and of there being no repository candidate and no materialization receipt for it. The legal identity question is closed; the mechanical path from a resolved identity to an exact source contract is named in residualBlockers and belongs to Session A.
